THIS WRIT PETITION IS FILED UNDER ARTICLE 226 OF THE CONSTITUTION OF INDIA PRAYING TO QUASH THE FIR IN CRIME NO. 32/2022 REGISTERED FOR THE OFFENCES PUNISHABLE UNDER SECTIONS 376, 498A 504, 506 AND 34 IPC AND SECTIONS 3 AND 4 OF DOWRY PROHIBITION ACT ON THE FILE OF PRINCIPAL CIVIL JUDGE AND JMFC PUTTUR D.K. PURUSANT TO THE POLICE COMPLAINT FILED BY RESPONDENT NO.2 AS PER ANNEXURE-A AND ETC.,
 THIS WRIT PETITION COMING ON FOR ADMISSION THIS DAY,
THE COURT PASSED THE FOLLOWING:

ORDER This petition is filed by the petitioner-accused No.1 under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. for quashing the FIR in Crime No.32 of 2022 registered by Kadaba Police Station, Puttur Rural Circle, for the offences punishable under Sections 376, 498A, 504 and 506 read with Section 34 of IPC and under Sections 3 and 4 of DP Act.

sentences.text:
2. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner, learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent No.1 - State and learned counsel for respondent No.2.
3.

The case of the prosecution is that, the complainant - respondent No.2 who is the victim lodged the complaint in the police station on 07.04.2022 alleging that the petitioner is said to be the relative and he came in contact with her and both of NC:
2024:KHC:14914 them fell in love and he is said to have sexually assaulted the victim against her will, due to which, she became pregnant.
Thereafter, she requested the petitioner to marry her.

The petitioner refused to marry and made an allegation that he is not the cause for her pregnancy and that he wants to perform DNA test to know whether he is the biological father of the child or not.

Subsequently, on 05.08.2021 she delivered a male child and thereafter at the intervention of family members of the petitioner and respondent No.2, on 15.11.2021, their marriage was performed and it was registered.
Subsequently, the accused started harassing her mentally stating that the child is not belonging to him and he was suspecting her character.

It is also alleged that the petitioner always used to continuously harass her by telling that he is an army man and he could have received more money as dowry and rich people were ready to give dowry for him and therefore, he demanded Deekshith Gowda.

sentences.text: Therefore, she has filed the complaint.
After registration of FIR, the police started investigation, which is under challenge.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner contended that the petitioner and respondent No.2 was major in age and they NC: 2024:KHC:14914 fell in love and there was consensual sex between them.
Therefore, the question of attracting Section 375 of IPC does not arise in order to say that he has committed the offence punishable under Section 376 of IPC.
There is inordinate delay in lodging the complaint.
Even prior to the marriage or at the time of marriage, there is no demand of dowry.
Therefore, there is no physical assault by the petitioner.
Hence, conducting investigation is nothing but abuse of process of law.

Hence, he prays for quashing the FIR.
5.

Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.2 contends that even if Section 376 of IPC is not attracted, the accused was harassing her physically and mentally for demand of dowry, abusing her in filthy language and threatening with dire consequences, which attracts Sections 498A, 504, 506 of IPC and he is continuously harassing the complainant by suspecting her character and birth of child and disputing paternity.
Therefore, the matter requires investigation.
6. Learned High Court Government Pleader supporting the contention of learned counsel for respondent No.2 prays for dismissal of the petition.
Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and on perusal of the FIR, which reveals that admittedly, the age of the victim was 21 years at the time of lodging the complaint.
As per the complainant, she fell in love with the petitioner and subsequently they had sex, due to which, she became pregnant.
Thereafter, she requested the petitioner to marry, for which, he refused.
He also suspected the paternity.
Thereafter, she delivered a child on 05.08.2021.
Subsequently, the accused married her.
8. On perusal of the said averments, which reveals that both the petitioner and the respondent are adults having consensual sex between them, due to which, she became pregnant.

It is not the case where the accused promised her to marry and thereafter, he committed sexual assault, but they are in love with each other and they had consensual sex, due to which, she became pregnant.

Thereafter,
she requested the petitioner to marry her, but he refused.
A false promise to marry cannot attract Sections 420 and 376 of IPC.

In catena of decisions of this Court and Hon'ble Supreme Court, the consensual sex between the two adults, cannot be considered as a sexual assault to attract Section 375 of IPC against her will NC: 2024:KHC:14914 or without her consent.
Therefore, as rightly contended by learned counsel for the petitioner, the offence under Section 376 of IPC is not attracted.
Even otherwise, subsequently, the petitioner has married the complainant.
Therefore, a false promise to marry does not arise.
9. However, the marriage between the petitioner and respondent No.2 was performed on 15.11.2021 and it was registered.
Thereafter, the petitioner started harassing her by making character assassination and disputing the paternity of the child and he also wants to perform DNA test to Deekshith Gowda.

sentences.text: He was also threatening her that he would file a case for damages against her and he was continuously pestering her that he is an army man and rich people were waiting to give their daughters to him on marriage and he could have got more dowry and said to have demanded dowry after the marriage.
However, there is no demand of dowry prior to marriage or at the time of marriage in order to attract Section 3 of DP Act.

It is only the accused started demanding dowry only after the marriage, which would attract Section 4 of DP Act and subsequently, in NC: 2024:KHC:14914 respect to meet unlawful demand of dowry which would attract Section 498A of IPC.

10. Even otherwise, the mental harassment, character assassination, abusing in filthy language and threatening with dire consequences by the accused would attract Sections 498A, 504 and 506 of IPC and Section 4 of DP Act.
Therefore, in my view, the matter requires investigation.
At this stage, the FIR cannot be quashed, even though the ingredients made under Section 376 of IPC is not attracted.

11. Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (i) The Criminal Petition is allowed in part.
(ii) The FIR against the petitioner for the offence punishable under Sections 376 of IPC and under Section 3 of DP Act is hereby quashed.
(iii) However, the police is directed to investigate the matter with regard to the other offences.

(iv) During investigation, the police are also permitted to make arrangements for conducting DNA test of the child to NC: 2024:KHC:14914 know the paternity of the child and to file final report in accordance with law.
